title.en: Define a register and a shift register
Explain SISO, SIPO, PISO and PIPO registers
Describe ring and Johnson counters and shifting as ×2 and ÷2

say.en: A USB cable sends a byte one bit at a time, but the computer needs all eight bits together. A row of flip-flops that passes bits along on each clock turns serial data into parallel and back. In this lesson: Define a register and a shift register.
Explain SISO, SIPO, PISO and PIPO registers.
Describe ring and Johnson counters and shifting as times 2 and divided by 2.

body.en: A register is a group of flip-flops that stores a binary word, one bit per flip-flop. In a *shift* register, D flip-flops are connected in cascade with a common clock: the output of each feeds the D input of the next, so on every clock pulse the stored bits move one place. By the way data enter and leave, there are four types: serial-in serial-out (SISO), serial-in parallel-out (SIPO), parallel-in serial-out (PISO) and parallel-in parallel-out (PIPO). Loading n bits serially needs n clock pulses.

points.en: Serial loading of n bits needs n clock pulses
Universal *shift* register (IC 74194): shift left/right, parallel load

title.en: Uses: conversion, arithmetic and ring counters

body.en: SIPO converts serial data to parallel and PISO converts parallel to serial (used in serial communication). Shifting a binary number one place left multiplies it by 2; shifting right divides it by 2. Feeding the last output back to the first input makes a ring counter: with n flip-flops it circulates a single 1 through n states (MOD-n). Feeding back the complement $\bar{Q}$ of the last stage gives a Johnson (twisted-ring) counter with 2n states (MOD-2n).

points.en: SIPO: serial → parallel; PISO: parallel → serial
Ring counter: n states; Johnson counter: 2n states

problem.en: A 4-bit SISO register is cleared to 0000. The data 1101 are entered MSB first (1, 1, 0, 1). Find Q0 Q1 Q2 Q3 after each clock pulse.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A 4-bit SISO register is cleared to 0000. The data 1101 are entered MSB first (1, 1, 0, 1). Find Q0 Q1 Q2 Q3 after each clock pulse.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A 4-bit SISO register is cleared to 0000. The data 1101 are entered MSB first (1, 1, 0, 1). Find Q0 Q1 Q2 Q3 after each clock pulse.
Clock 1: 1 enters gives 1000.
Clock 2: 1 enters gives 1100.
Clock 3: 0 enters gives 0110.
Clock 4: 1 enters gives 1011.
So the answer is Q0Q1Q2Q3 equals 1000, 1100, 0110, 1011.

problem.en: An 8-bit register holds 00001010 (10). It is shifted left twice. What does it hold now?

steps.en: No 1 has been lost from the left end, so the result is exact.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. An 8-bit register holds 00001010 (10). It is shifted left twice. What does it hold now?

say.en: Let us work this out together. An 8-bit register holds 00001010 10. It is shifted left twice. What does it hold now?
Shift left once: 00010100 equals 20 times 2.
Shift left again: 00101000 equals 40 times 2.
No 1 has been lost from the left end, so the result is exact.
So the answer is 00101000 equals 40.
